keyVerseText: And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. Peter: this name signifies a rock
rootMeaning: The word ἐκκλησία (ekklēsía) is derived from the Greek preposition ἐκ (ek), meaning 'out of' or 'from,' combined with a derivative of καλέω (kaleō), meaning 'to call.' Thus, its root meaning is 'a calling out' or 'an assembly summoned out.' This literal sense highlights the concept of a group of people called out from among others to gather for a specific purpose, beyond the general idea of any gathering or crowd.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, ἐκκλησία appears 115 times and is most commonly translated as 'the church' (39 occurrences), reflecting its primary New Testament usage as the community of Christian believers. It also appears in forms such as 'of the church,' 'the churches,' and 'unto the churches,' indicating both local assemblies and the universal body of believers. This consistency in translation underscores the term's focus on a distinct, divinely summoned community rather than a generic congregation.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἐκκλησία as a 'called-out assembly' enriches our grasp of the church’s identity as a people specifically summoned by God, not merely a social or religious club. This calling sets the church apart as a holy community with a divine purpose, reflecting continuity with the Jewish assembly while embodying the new covenant in Christ. The term conveys both the corporate nature of the church and its spiritual unity, emphasizing that the church is built on Christ as the foundation and is sustained by God’s sovereign call. This highlights the church’s role as a visible expression of God’s kingdom on earth.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 16:18, Jesus declares, 'upon this rock I will build my church,' using ἐκκλησία to signify the community He establishes. The word here conveys not just any assembly but a divinely called and founded body, secured against the powers of hell. This reflects the church’s enduring nature and divine protection, rooted in Christ as the foundation and the calling that defines its very existence.
